tagline: A national operator of outpatient physical therapy clinics and provider of industrial injury prevention services
hero_kpi_rationale: The clinic count is the primary indicator of USPH's size and trajectory of organic and acquisition-driven growth, a key driver of its business model.

kpis.name: Clinic Count
kpis.explanation: Total number of physical clinics operated or managed by USPH.
kpis.description: Clinic count reached 780 at end of 2025, up 59 units versus 761 at end of 2024 (of which 746 owned and 34 managed).
kpis.signal: Sustained growth via acquisitions and strategic alliances

kpis.name: Net Patient Medicare Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from Medicare patients, a key segment of the customer base.
kpis.description: Net patient Medicare revenue reached $213.5M in 2025, versus $183.4M in 2024, driven by clinic portfolio growth.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Consolidated gross margin, reflecting operational profitability of services.
kpis.description: Consolidated gross margin reaches 19.2% in 2025 ($149.7M gross profit on $780.9M net revenue), compared to 18.4% in 2024.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating income divided by total revenue.
kpis.description: Operating margin is not provided in the excerpts.

kpis.name: R&D Investments (% revenue)
kpis.explanation: Research and development spending relative to revenue.
kpis.description: USPH does not conduct significant R&D in the technology sense.
kpis.signal: Not applicable to physical therapy care sector

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Spending on physical or technology assets.
kpis.description: Capex is not detailed in the excerpts.

kpis.name: Headcount (employees)
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the company.
kpis.description: Employee count is not provided in the excerpts.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of $1.2B in latest year

kpis.name: Medicare Reimbursement Rate Change YoY
kpis.explanation: Year-over-year change in Medicare reimbursement rates for therapy services.
kpis.description: Medicare reimbursement declined 2.9% in 2025 versus 2024, following a 1.8% reduction in 2024.

kpis.name: Clinics Integrated via Strategic Alliances
kpis.explanation: Number of clinics integrated into new strategic alliances with hospital systems.
kpis.description: In February 2026, two strategic alliances announced covering 70 clinics (60 in New York + 10 local), integrated into hospital care networks over 10 years.

risks.title: Medicare Reimbursement Reduction
risks.score_rationale: This risk is at the top of the 10-K document, mentioned at the opening of risk factors. Language is strong: 'materially affect,' 'not sufficiently offset,' 'not cover costs.' Medicare dependence is high (32.8% of revenue in 2025: $213.5M/$650.4M) and growing. Regulation category is heavily weighted here.

risks.title: Retrospective Audits and Payment Recoveries
risks.score_rationale: Text emphasizes retroactive adjustments, recovery actions, post-payment audits on the rise, and legal obligations to reimburse overpayments. Mention of severe penalties, including fines and program exclusion. Central position in the document with concerning language.

risks.title: Dependence on Private Payers
risks.score_rationale: Total net patient revenue $650.4M in 2025; Medicare $213.5M = 32.8%; thus private revenue approximately $436.9M = 67.2% of patient revenue. Text mentions growing pressure to reduce reimbursement and contracts at reduced rates. Risk of patient loss or margin compression if contracts are not renewed. Less existential than Medicare but structural.

risks.title: Non-Compliance with HIPAA/HITECH Obligations
risks.score_rationale: Text describes strict obligations for patient data security and confidentiality. Explicit mention of civil/criminal penalties, class action lawsuits, and mitigation costs following a breach. HIPAA is a critical regulatory pillar for healthcare actors.

risks.title: Health Crisis or Pandemic
risks.score_rationale: Risk is explicitly tied to pandemics, with direct operational effects: staff loss, appointment cancellation. Mention of economic uncertainty and capital access. Strong forward-looking language ('adverse impact'), but less frequent than regulatory risks.

risks.title: Medicaid Reimbursement Pressure
risks.score_rationale: Text emphasizes federal and state pressure to contain Medicaid spending. Specific mention of non-expansion in certain states like Texas. Risk of rate cuts or coverage loss, similar to Medicare but with lower exposure (Medicaid revenue not specified but included in the 67% private).

risks.title: Put Right Repurchase Obligations
risks.score_rationale: Text describes contractual put rights requiring share purchases at a price based on earnings multiple, potentially above fair value. Explicit mention of default risk if financing is insufficient. Structural financial risk tied to acquisition growth.

risks.title: Debt and Financial Constraints
risks.score_rationale: Debt risk tied to active acquisition strategy is mentioned in risk factors. Growth through acquisitions (49 clinics added in 2025) creates financing obligations and debt covenants.

ai_positioning.summary: USPH has not mentioned artificial intelligence, machine learning, or similar terms in the excerpts provided from its 10-K/20-F documents. Therefore, its positioning on AI cannot be determined from this information.
